packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Transcribe what you can see, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

The transcription retains apparent bars and raised letters where I can distinguish them: ē, vocā?, sᵈ?, autē?, q̄m?, vē?, sᵒ?, aliū?. These are visual approximations of the marks, not assured character identifications. A possible expansion of autē? is aut(em)?; the other abbreviations are left unexpanded. The apparent long s in miſtio? is uncertain. Question marks apply to the preceding word or abbreviated group. No grammatical reconstruction has been supplied for unreadable groups.

Physical layout and limitations
There is one horizontal crop, containing three main physical lines of writing. The numbering counts these lines from top to bottom. The left edge is dark and damaged, particularly around the beginnings of the lines. The right edge limits the endings, and portions of the final line's descending strokes meet the bottom crop. Ink contrast varies, and several letters and abbreviation marks are difficult to separate from surface texture. The third line is particularly uncertain in this reading. The image does not establish a wider column order. No separate marginal text or confidently recognizable deletion or insertion is visible. Red-colored marks occur within the third line toward the right; I cannot confidently distinguish their textual function. There are no other supplied crops, and therefore no observed overlap to account for.
